title: uber/ADR — ADR secures enterprise AI agents through observability, security benchmarking, and threat detection. Deployed at Uber.
content:
ADR (Agentic AI Detection and Response) is an enterprise security system for AI agents. It helps organizations secure employee-facing agents such as Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot CLI, and DeepSeek Harness, as well as customer-facing agents such as AI support agents.
ADR is deployed in production at Uber, and the accompanying paper was accepted to MLSys 2026: Paper PDF · Slides PDF
ADR secures enterprise AI agents through five complementary capabilities: discovering unsanctioned AI tools, observing agent activity, evaluating defenses, detecting threats, and preventing unsafe actions.
- ADR Discovery: Find the AI tools present on employee endpoints. Inventories installed AI applications, CLI agents, IDE extensions, local model runtimes, and MCP servers, and flags unknown surfaces for review.
- ADR Observability: Understand what AI agents are doing and why. In production, ADR captures agent intent, tool use, and execution traces across 7+ AI coding tools on macOS, Linux, and Windows, as well as internal automation and customer-facing support agents.
- ADR Benchmark: Test agent security under realistic enterprise conditions. ADR-Bench includes 300+ tasks, 134 MCP servers, and coverage of all 17 agent attack techniques.
- ADR Detection: Detect risky agent behavior efficiently. Its two-tier architecture combines high-recall triage with deeper agentic reasoning for suspicious sessions.
- ADR Prevention: Stop unsafe actions before they cause harm. This component is not included in the current open-source release. Stay tuned.
This repository contains the open-source ADR Discovery, ADR Sensor, ADR-Bench, and ADR Detector described in the paper. The offline ADR Explorer engine, which hardens ADR Detection through pre-deployment red teaming, is not included here.
git clone https://github.com/uber/ADR
cd ADR/Detection
uv sync
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="..." OPENAI_API_KEY="..."
Default detector is adr (ADR dual-agent). For keyless smoke tests, use --detector llamafirewall (see Detection/README.md).
See docs/REPRODUCIBILITY.md for the full evaluation workflow (inflate packed benchmark → run detectors → plot figures).
Component documentation:
ADR Sensor also captures Gemini CLI session journals on macOS, Linux, and Windows, including tool results and nested subagent sessions.
- Discovery/README.md: endpoint inventory, probes, and the fingerprint catalog
- Sensor/README.md: telemetry collection and unified schema
- Detection/README.md: ADR-Bench, detector baselines, MCP infrastructure

report.summary: Uber open-sources ADR, a production-deployed system that discovers, observes, benchmarks, and detects threats against enterprise AI agents.
report.background: Enterprise adoption of AI coding agents such as Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot CLI, and DeepSeek Harness has outpaced the security tooling designed to govern them. Employees install unsanctioned tools and MCP servers, agents inherit broad credentials, and prompt-injection or tool-abuse attacks can trigger real file writes, network calls, and data exfiltration. Traditional EDR and SIEM products lack the semantic hooks to interpret agent intent, tool invocations, and multi-step execution traces, leaving a blind spot between endpoint security and LLM guardrails. Research interest has surged too: benchmark suites like AgentDojo and attack taxonomies now catalogue dozens of agent-specific techniques. Uber's ADR, accepted to MLSys 2026, packages lessons from running such defenses in production rather than a lab, making it one of the first vendor-neutral, openly licensed reference architectures for agentic AI detection and response.
key_points: ADR bundles five complementary capabilities: Discovery (inventorying installed AI apps, CLI agents, IDE extensions, local model runtimes, and MCP servers), Observability (capturing intent, tool use, and execution traces), Benchmark (ADR-Bench), Detection (identifying risky behavior), and Prevention (blocking unsafe actions before harm). Each maps to a familiar SOC workflow, making adoption easier for security teams.

ADR-Bench is the headline research artifact: over 300 tasks, 134 MCP servers, and coverage of all 17 known agent attack techniques. It lets teams red-team their own agent deployments under realistic enterprise conditions before production rollout, rather than relying on generic LLM jailbreak suites that ignore tool-use and environment context.

ADR is deployed at Uber and is cross-platform. The sensor collects telemetry from 7+ AI coding tools across macOS, Linux, and Windows, monitors internal automation and customer-facing support agents, and captures Gemini CLI session journals including tool results and nested subagent sessions — a level of depth most open-source agent monitors lack.

Detection uses a two-tier architecture: a high-recall triage layer cheaply flags suspicious sessions, then a deeper agentic reasoning pass investigates them. This design balances cost and accuracy, avoiding the common failure mode of running expensive LLM reasoning over every single agent action in an enterprise fleet.

The open-source release is deliberately partial. Discovery, Sensor, ADR-Bench, and Detector ship under Apache 2.0, but the offline ADR Explorer engine and the Prevention component (blocking unsafe actions) are withheld, signaling commercial or roadmap value Uber intends to retain.
report.impact: For the AI industry, ADR legitimizes 'agentic AI detection and response' as a distinct security category alongside LLM firewalls and AI gateways, and gives vendors a production-tested blueprint to benchmark against. For developers, it provides an immediately usable sensor schema, detector baselines, and a reproducible evaluation workflow, letting teams measure whether their agents leak credentials or obey injected instructions without building infrastructure from scratch. For regular users, the practical effect is safer autonomous agents: fewer silent data exfiltration events, better audit trails when an agent misbehaves, and eventually hard blocks on dangerous tool calls. The main limitation is that Prevention is closed, so teams get visibility and detection, not enforcement, out of the box.
report.tools: Start with the uber/ADR repo itself: Detection/README.md documents ADR-Bench and detector baselines, and docs/REPRODUCIBILITY.md walks through inflating the benchmark, running detectors, and plotting results. Meta's LlamaFirewall serves as a keyless smoke-test detector. Watch AgentDojo, vendored inside the repo, for agent attack evaluations; OWASP's LLM/Agentic Top 10 for threat taxonomy; and MCP server tooling for inventory. If you need enforcement, pair ADR detection with an agent gateway or policy layer.
